mechanism_narrative: The continued rebound in WORKPLACES mobility over the last four weeks will lift RETAIL_REC over the next month because more commuting increases weekday shopping and lunch-trip demand. The effect should appear within 4 weeks and remain visible as long as workplace mobility keeps recovering.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 4-week average despite WORKPLACES staying above its t-1w level for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated and keeps falling week by week, households spend less time at home and more time outside, which pushes RETAIL_REC higher over the next 2 weeks. The signal should weaken if residential time stops declining.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 2 points week-on-week from its current level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after a further week-over-week drop in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: A stronger PARKS rebound combined with lower TRANSIT use indicates local, non-transit leisure activity replacing long-distance trips, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior 4-week average over the next month. This mechanism works when park visits rise while transit remains subdued.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS continues to increase and TRANSIT stays below -35.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above the -40% threshold, the city has likely entered a deeper reopening phase in which access constraints ease and shopping trips recover quickly. That threshold crossing should raise RETAIL_REC within 1 week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -40% after being below -40%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week after TRANSIT first moves above -40%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in GROCERY_PHARM after its recent improvement implies fewer essential errand trips and a broader normalization of household routines, which should spill over into higher retail-and-recreation activity over the next 4 weeks. The effect is strongest once grocery mobility is no longer in double-digit negative territory.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above -15% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or falls over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above -15% for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS continues to rise while WORKPLACES keeps recovering, the combined relaxation of leisure and work activity will pull shopping trips higher after about 2 weeks. Retail recreation should respond only when both series move upward together, not when either rises alone.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days when PARKS and WORKPLACES both post another weekly gain.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, a further weakening of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES will precede lower RETAIL_REC over the next 4 weeks because fewer commuting and discretionary trips reduce exposure to shopping districts. This prediction holds only in a restriction-tightening regime.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain below their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: The recent summer-style rise in PARKS mobility should gradually displace enclosed shopping activity and keep RETAIL_REC below the last 4-week average over the next month. The effect is seasonal and should be visible even if other categories stay stable.
evidence_refs: fact:parks moved from -20.9 at t-3w to 19.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying positive.
